payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold, retracting the earlier higher claim. The cell delivered 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density. At projected 500 MWh production scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The dopant precipitates in cold conditions, creating a hard operating-temperature floor of 4 °C, below which cycling must stop.
